full_judgment:
Md Hassan Ameen J: This Rule was issued on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused petitioner Shahidul calling upon the opposite party, State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna, to show cause as to why the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 28-9-97 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 7, Khulna in Special Tribunal Case (STC) No.227 of 1996 arising out of GR No. 441 of 1996 corresponding to Khulna PS Case No. 37 dated 27-4-1996 should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The accused petitioner and others were placed on trial before the court of Special Tribunal No. 7, Khulna in Special Tribunal Case No. 227 of 1996 and after conclusion of trial the learned Tribunal by the judgment and order dated 28-9-97 convicted the accused petitioner and 2 others under section 4 of the Explosive Substances Act and sentenced each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for l0(ten) years and also to pay a fine of Taka 500.00 in default to suffer simple imprisonment for 3(three) months more. 

 3. The prosecution story, in brief, is that, on 27-4-1996 at 23,55 hours SI Md. Abul Bashar as informant lodged a first information report with the Khulna police station against the accused petitioner and 2 others alleging, inter alia, that on 27-4-1996 at 23,00 hours the informant was on patrol duty while he reached in front of NK Food. Tutpara main road found 3(three) youths in suspicious movement. Those 3(three) youths tried to run away when challenged but one accused namely AI Amin was caught red-handed and after search police recovered 2 live bombs from him. The said accused confessed that accused Shahidul (accused petitioner) and Noor Islam were with him who fled away earlier. Accordingly, the informant lodged the first information report when the aforesaid PS case was started. 

 4. The police after investigation submitted charge sheet against the accused petitioner and 2 others under section 4 of the Explosive Substances Act. The case ultimately came to the file of the present tribunal on transfer who framed charge under section 4 of the Explosive Substances Act which was read over and explained in Bengali to the accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and demanded trial. 

 5. The prosecution examined 7 witnesses and after close of the prosecution witnesses the learned Tribunal examined the accused persons except the accused petitioner who was in hajat in connection with another case. The defence did not examine any DW on their behalf. The defence case, as could be gathered from the trend of cross examination, is total denial. Their inter alia, case is that nothing was recovered from their control and possession but they have been falsely implicated in this case. 

 6. After closes of the prosecution case the learned Tribunal in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case convicted the accused petitioner and others for the offence charged and sentenced them thereunder as above vide judgment and order dated 28-9-97. Being aware about the same while in custody the accused petitioner filed the present case for quashment of the impugned judgment, order of conviction and sentence. 

 8. Mahmud Hossain, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, however opposed the Rule alleging, inter alia, that the impugned judgment and order of conviction have been passed against the accused petitioner. and others on the basis of evidence on record and that the accused petitioner having absconded after attending court for some time clearly indicates his guilty mind and accordingly, the impugned judgment and order of conviction deserves no interference. He lastly submits that the learned trial Court based its finding on the averments of co-accused and that the accused petitioner being member of the same gang who had opportunity to flee away from the place of occurrence when one of his companions was apprehended by police and accordingly, he contends that the present case does not come under the mischief of section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 9. A convict may invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 561A CrPC if he can make out a case of coram non judice of the trial Court or that the facts alleged do not constitute any criminal offence or that the conviction has been based on no legal evidence or otherwise for securing the ends of justice. The latest decision on exercise of inherent jurisdiction by this court under section 561A CrPC in 46 DLR (AD) 67 where our Appellate Division has held the High Court Division may exercise its inherent power to quash a proceeding or even a conviction on conclusion of trial where the court concerned got no jurisdiction to hold the said trial or the facts alleged against the accused do not constitute any criminal offence or the conviction has been based on no legal evidence or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. That is also the view of our Appellate Division vide 45 DLR (AD) 175. 

 10. Before entering into merit of this case it may be mentioned here that the impugned judgment and order of conviction was passed against the accused petitioner in his absence inasmuch as the accused petitioner though surrendered before the trial Court but remained absent after getting bail, as such, he could not be examined under section 342 CrPC after close of the prosecution witnesses but it is a matter of regret that the annexures filed by the accused petitioner indicate that the accused petitioner was apprehended in connection with another case and put into hajat while the learned trial Court examined the other 2 accused persons under section 342 CrPC and his presence in court was beyond his control. It is needless to mention here that provision of section 342 CrPC has been codified by the legislature providing opportunity to the accused concerned to make out his case about his innocence of the offence charged. In the present case it appears that the accused petitioner was denied his right to present his case at the time of examination of the other accused for no fault of his own as he was in Government custody. So, it appears that the accused petitioner has been prejudiced in the matter since he could not make out his case in the matter of denial of the offence charged against him. It has been set at rest by this Court and also by our Appellate Division that under Arms Act it must be shown that the accused is in the actual possession and not in the constructive possession of that particular person charged i.e. actual and physical possession and control and not merely a possession or control by construction of law. It is not a liability to be found in a merely constructive or presumed possession or control which the law might for other purposes import into the facts of the case it is incumbent upon the prosecution to give good evidence that such arms are in exclusive possession and control of the particular member of the party who is sought to be charged with his possession. Regard being had to the above facts and circumstances let us examine the evidence on record. 

 11. The PW 1 Md. Tomijuddin, SI of Police of concerned patrol party, PW 2, SI of Police another member of the said patrol party of the informant and PW 3, SI Abul Bashar the informant of this case have said in a voice about their patrol duty on the date, time, place and apprehension of one of the accused namely, Al-Amin in the manner as alleged by the prosecution. They have further corroborated each-other about recovery of 2 live bombs from the control and possession of apprehended accused Al-Amin on the date of seizure of the same in presence of the witnesses by preparation of a seizure list and finally they have said that the apprehended accused namely, Al-Amin reported that the 2 accused persons fled away from the place of occurrence at the time of his (accused Al-Amin) apprehension, are Shahidul and Nurul Islam. The defence failed to discredit them in any way by cross. 

 14. The PW 7, the final investigation officer of this case, has said about the investigation of the case. He claimed that while serving at Khulna PS he started the aforesaid Khulna PS case on receipt of written FIR along with seized alamats, seizure list and the apprehended accused Al-Amin and SI Abul Bashar was appointed investigation officer of this case but on his (Abul Bashar) transfer he (deponent) was appointed investigation officer of this case. He further said that he received the case diary, alamats and other papers of the former investigation officer and examined the same and being satisfied submitted charge sheet against the accused persons under section 4 of the Explosive Substances Act since prima facie case was made out against them. He proved the ejahar, First Information Report form and his signature thereon Exts.1/2, 1(a)/2 and the sketch map of the place of occurrence with Index along with his (previous investigation officer) signature Ext. 3, 3/1, 4 and 4/1 respectively. This is all about the evidence on record. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute but without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence so much so relates to the accused petitioner is hereby quashed. The accused petitioner namely, Shahidul, son of A. Mannan of South Totpara, Police Station and District Khulna be set at liberty at once, if not wanted in any other case, Send down a copy of judgment along with the LC record to the trial Court for information and necessary action.
